mechanism_narrative: A higher current value of the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) signals elevated inflation, which typically leads to reduced equity valuations due to higher real interest rates and increased risk aversion, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL is above the 50th percentile of its historical distribution.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.1 percentage points above 9.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, prompting expectations of Federal Reserve rate cuts and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 9.0% and monthly change exceeds 0.1pp.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of unemployment rate exceeding 9.0% and industrial production falling below 90 (both relative to their recent levels) indicates a severe economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate recession and policy responses.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 9.0 and INDPRO < 90.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening regime (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals economic contraction under high interest rates, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5 and INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A higher current value of housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust residential construction activity, which is a leading indicator of consumer spending and economic expansion, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST is above the 50th percentile of its historical distribution.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95 (index value) indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which typically leads to negative equity market returns as the economy faces contraction risks over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 95.

mechanism_narrative: A higher current value of non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) indicates robust job growth, which typically boosts consumer confidence and spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS is above the 50th percentile of its historical distribution.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 0.3 percentage points indicates accelerating inflation, prompting expectations of Federal Reserve rate hikes and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL monthly change exceeds 0.3%.
